scenario.title: 公司尾牙：致詞、抽獎、跟主管聊天
scenario.context: 第六章的收尾：外商公司的尾牙。你要跟老闆聊過去一年、用委婉的方式提建議、上台簡短致詞，還要應付抽獎和敬酒。這一章的 used to、連接詞、軟化語氣、What 子句都會派上用場。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I am, thanks. I'm still not used to seeing everyone this dressed up, though.
lines.zh: 很開心，謝謝。不過我還是不習慣看到大家打扮成這樣。

lines.speaker: Director
lines.en: Ha! So, how's your first year been?
lines.zh: 哈！那你第一年過得如何？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Honestly, it's been great. I used to worry about fitting in, but the team has been amazing.
lines.zh: 說真的很棒。我以前擔心融不進去，但團隊很棒。

lines.speaker: Director
lines.en: Glad to hear it. Anything we could do better?
lines.zh: 很高興聽到。有什麼我們可以做得更好的嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Well, it might be worth having clearer approval steps. What slows us down most is waiting for sign-off.
lines.zh: 嗯，也許可以考慮讓核准流程更清楚。最拖慢我們的是等簽核。

lines.speaker: Director
lines.en: That's fair. However, I think we've improved since the new system. Let's discuss it in January.
lines.zh: 有道理。不過我覺得用了新系統後有改善了。我們一月再討論。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Sounds great. Thanks for being such a good sport about the feedback.
lines.zh: 好的。謝謝你這麼有風度接受回饋。

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.en: Minz, will you say a few words for the design team?
lines.zh: Minz，可以代表設計團隊說幾句話嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Hi everyone. This year was tough. Although we had some crazy deadlines, we never let each other down.
lines.zh: 大家好。今年很辛苦。雖然有一些瘋狂的截止日，但我們從沒讓彼此失望。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: What I'm most proud of isn't a single project. It's how we supported each other.
lines.zh: 我最自豪的不是某個案子，而是我們怎麼互相扶持。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: We've been on a roll since the summer, so let's keep it going. Please raise a glass to the team!
lines.zh: 我們從夏天開始就一路順風，讓我們繼續保持。請大家為團隊舉杯！

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: Nice speech. Now let your hair down and enjoy the night!
lines.zh: 講得好。現在放輕鬆好好享受今晚吧！

patterns.en: I'd like to say a few words.
I couldn't have done it without ___.
What I'm most proud of is ___.
Thanks for all your hard work.

chinglish.wrong: Thank you boss, boss is very good.
chinglish.right: Thanks, Karen. You've been an amazing manager.
chinglish.why: 英文不用 boss 當稱呼。直接叫名字並具體稱讚。

chinglish.right: Thanks for all your hard work. Enjoy the night!
chinglish.why: 中文口號式的致詞直翻缺主詞動詞，聽起來不完整。

chinglish.wrong: Although this year is hard, but we did it.
chinglish.right: Although this year was hard, we did it.
chinglish.why: 複習第 53 單元：although 和 but 只能選一個；而且今年已經過去，用 was。
英文敬酒用 Cheers。Bottoms up（第 80 單元）才是「乾杯喝光」，但外國人通常不會逼你喝完。

grammar.title: used to、連接詞、軟化語氣
grammar.oneLiner: 職場進階的三個工具：用 used to / be used to 講改變、用連接詞組織論點、用軟化語氣提建議。
whenToUse: 講過去與現在的對比：I used to worry… / I'm not used to… / I've gotten used to…
組織論點：Although…, … / However, … / Therefore, … / What I'm most proud of is…
委婉建議：It might be worth… / You might want to… / It'd be great if…
描述成就：We launched… / We've grown by…（第 51 單元）
未來目標：By next year, we'll have…（第 56 單元）
補充說明：Karen, who led the project, …（第 57 單元）
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 這一章的每個文法點都和「職場溝通的分寸」有關：中文靠語氣和關係拿捏分寸，英文則靠句型。尾牙這種場合同時需要正式（致詞）、委婉（跟主管提建議）、輕鬆（跟同事聊天），是練習切換語域的好機會。第 85 單元會更系統地講語域。

examples.correct: I used to hate public speaking, but I'm getting used to it.
examples.note: used to + V vs get used to + V-ing。

examples.correct: Although we missed one deadline, we delivered every project.
examples.incorrect: Although we missed one deadline, but we delivered every project.
examples.note: although 和 but 選一個。

examples.correct: It might be worth hiring another designer next year.
What made this year special was the team.
By next December, we'll have doubled our client list.

quiz.question: I ___ nervous at parties, but now I enjoy them.
It was a hard year. ___, we grew by 20%.
___ I'm most grateful for is this team.
Which is the most diplomatic suggestion?
options: It might be worth reviewing the process.
quiz.explanation: It might be worth… 委婉。

quiz.question: I'm still getting used to ___ (give) speeches.

slang.usage: Let's raise a glass to… = 讓我們為…舉杯。

examples.en: Let's raise a glass to the happy couple.
Please raise a glass to Karen for an amazing year.
examples.zh: 請大家為 Karen 帶來精彩的一年舉杯。

slang.usage: 平常很正經的人放開來玩。

examples.en: It's the year-end party. Let your hair down!
It's nice to see the boss let her hair down for once.
examples.zh: 難得看到老闆放輕鬆，真好。

slang.meaning: 有風度的人、玩得起的人
slang.usage: 願意配合、輸了或被開玩笑也不生氣的人。Be a good sport.

examples.en: Thanks for being a good sport about the costume.
examples.zh: 謝謝你願意配合穿那套服裝。

examples.en: He lost the game but was a good sport about it.
examples.zh: 他輸了比賽，但很有風度。

examples.en: We've won three pitches in a row. We're on a roll!
examples.zh: 我們連續拿下三個提案，一路順風！

examples.en: Don't stop now. You're on a roll.

review.question: ___ I love about this team is the trust.
review.explanation: 複習第 59 單元：What 子句。

review.question: I'm not used to ___ in front of people.
review.explanation: 複習第 58 單元：be used to + V-ing。

review.question: Our CEO, ___ started the company in 2010, gave a speech.
review.explanation: 複習第 57 單元：非限定子句。

review.question: By next year, we ___ fifty new clients.
review.explanation: 複習第 56 單元：未來完成式。

review.question: Who came up ___ the idea for the party theme?
review.explanation: 複習第 55 單元：come up with。

review.question: Which feedback is softest?
options: The speech might have been a bit long.
review.explanation: 複習第 54 單元：軟化語氣。

review.question: Which is correct?
options: Although it was hard, but we won.
Although it was hard, we won.
review.explanation: 複習第 53 單元：although 不配 but。

review.question: The bonus will ___ be announced next week.
I recommend ___ the dumplings. They're amazing.
I ___ (give) my speech when the mic stopped working.
review.explanation: 複習第 28 單元：被打斷的背景用過去進行式。

review.question: We've won three awards this year. We're on a ___!
review.explanation: on a roll = 一路順風。
